thread:
Carmen: quick heads-up — canary bring-up for Argos-v2 (int8 PTQ) shows a spike in funcall/structured-output parse failures. parse_fail rate ~7.8% vs fp16 baseline ~0.3%. saving a few repros and logs below.

Ben: link? :eyes:

Carmen: paste of a problematic exchange (trimmed):
```
REQUEST: {
  \u0022prompt\u0022: \u0022Call tool get_user_profile with id=123\u0022,
  \u0022function_call\u0022: {
    \u0022name\u0022: \u0022get_user_profile\u0022,
    \u0022arguments\u0022: \u0022{\u0022user_id\u0022: 123, \u0022fields\u0022: [\u0022email\u0022, \u0022name\u0022]}\u0022
  }
}

RESPONSE TOKENS (streamed):
... \u0022function_call\u0022: {
  \u0022name\u0022: \u0022get_user_profile\u0022,
  \u0022arguments\u0022: \u0022{\u0022user_id\u0022: 123, \u0022fields\u0022: [\u0022email\u0022, \u0022name\u0022]}\u0022
}
...
```
Problem: the model sometimes emits the arguments as a double-escaped JSON string (string-of-json) and sometimes as an object; our strict parser expects an object. also several traces show truncated suffix (missing closing brace) when kvcache prefix gets large.

Alice: interesting — in a few previous PTQ runs we saw extra trailing commas and unescaped newlines in structured output when temp>0.5. canary config had temp=0.6 for diversity.

Ryan: telemetry snapshot: canary sample size 5000, failures 389 => 7.78%. fp16 mirror over same sample: 14 failures => 0.28%. avg toolcall token_len +12% on int8 (so more tokens, more opportunities to hit cutoffs). routing: PTQ pool selected for lower cost.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary routed Argos-v2:int8 to ptq-pool at 02:14 UTC.

Ben: sometimes we get NDJSON-like stream with an empty line between objects; our NDJSON loader fails hard on that (null entry). also double-escaped JSON will parse as string and then we need a second pass to parse inner JSON.

Carmen: proposed mitigations: 1) soft-retry + tolerant parser in canary only (strip trailing commas, try JSON.parse twice if value is a string) 2) pin rollout to fp16 until we root-cause quant kernel/tokenization mismatch 3) add targeted goldens that stress nested objects and long arrays to canary.

Alice: +1 for rescue parser in canary. cheap heuristics first: unescapea = try(JSON.parse(x)) if fails, try fixing trailing commas and single quotes, then try parse again. but we should record whether rescue changed semantics (attach original string to telemetry).

Ben: also add micro-benchmark: 1k structured-output toolcall prompts comparing int8 vs fp16 measuring parse_fail, latency, tokens, token_cutoff_count. I'll sketch the harness.

Ryan: I can run the micro-bench tonight and push results to the canary dashboard. quick triage Q: is this more likely tokenizer-alignment (off-by-one) or kernel-induced token emission differences? logs show many traces where last_token != '}' — suggests truncation on streaming boundary.

Carmen: sample truncated response attached (single-line):
```
... \u0022function_call\u0022: {\u0022name\u0022:\u0022get_user_profile\u0022,\u0022arguments\u0022:{\u0022user_id\u0022:123,\u0022fields\u0022:[\u0022email\u0022,\u0022name\u0022]
```
Notice missing closing braces.

Ben: compilers team pushed a kernel tiling change last week — pinging @DevOps / @compilers to see if any PTQ codepath changed token emission or padding.

DevOps: incident-bot: created INF-2026-112 Argos-v2 int8 parse regression (assign: eng-ml + compilers).

Alice: short plan: (a) deploy canary-only rescue parser (b) run micro-bench 1k prompt suite int8 vs fp16 (c) if parse_fail > 1% after rescue, pin to fp16 and block wider rollout. Also add per-request flag indicating if rescue applied.

Ryan: noted. I'll add a dashboard tile showing pre- and post-rescue parse_fail and avg extra tokens consumed by rescue attempts.

Carmen: I'll open PR for the rescue parser + unit tests and add the new goldens set (small, focused on nested funcall objects). assigning @Alice and @Ben for review.

Ben: Thanks — I'll also add a tiny fuzzer that injects escaped/unescaped variants and NDJSON blank-line cases into the harness.

Alice: one more note — keep an eye on retry budget. we can't blindly retry N times for every request; cost and latency impact. prefer cheap in-place repairs before full retry.

Carmen: agreed. low-cost transforms first, then one canonical retry to fp16 mirror if rescue fails.

Ben: ok locked plan. tagging this thread with :mag: for follow-up.

DevOps: rolling back wider rollout for Argos-v2 until triage completes.

Carmen: thanks all — adding follow-ups to the ticket. I'll post bench results when Ryan uploads them.
